panels.title: Memory composition: what working set is actually made of
What working set is made of, by namespace
panels.description: cAdvisor's working set is the cgroup's charged memory minus INACTIVE file cache (cgroup v2: memory.current - inactive_file). container_memory_rss is the cgroup's anon counter -- anonymous pages only, not ps-style RSS -- so working set minus RSS is NOT page cache. It is active file cache plus kernel memory (slab, socket buffers, kernel stacks, tmpfs), of which only part is reclaimable. Working set is what the kubelet evicts and OOM-kills on, so it is the operationally meaningful figure. Columns B+C+D sum to A; E is already excluded from A.

targets.expr: (sum by (namespace) (container_memory_working_set_bytes{container!="",container!="POD",namespace=~"$namespace"}) - sum by (namespace) (container_memory_rss{container!="",container!="POD",namespace=~"$namespace"}) - (sum by (namespace) (container_memory_cache{container!="",container!="POD",namespace=~"$namespace"}) - (sum by (namespace) (container_memory_usage_bytes{container!="",container!="POD",namespace=~"$namespace"}) - sum by (namespace) (container_memory_working_set_bytes{container!="",container!="POD",namespace=~"$namespace"}))))

panels.title: Usage by owner (expand a row for their deployments)
panels.description: Owner rows aggregate their namespaces; expand one to see each deployment with its product. Owner is user.id, allocated per environment database, so keep the environment filter set when comparing owners. Clicking an owner, product or namespace filters the whole dashboard to it. CPU time is vCPU-hours consumed over the selected range -- the integral of the cores column, and what the ledger would bill on.
